name: Proud Bird gold tail (1985)
description: Continental's Saul Bass scheme as worn in 1985: an all-white body with two level stripes along it, a gold one above the cabin windows over a broader red-orange one through them, running from the nose to the tail. Behind the last door the gold sweeps up to the fin along a line parallel to the fin's leading edge, so the tail's upper body and the fin are gold, with a white band along the fin's leading edge. On the fin the 'meatball' big in black: a disc cut by six gold lines that start close together at its forward edge and fan out aft. 'CONTINENTAL' in upright extended black capitals over the forward windows, a small red meatball ahead of it and a US flag behind. Gray wings; engines as the type wears them (white on the 727 and DC-9, bare metal on the DC-10's and the A300's wing engines).

notes: Measured 2026-11-26 for ghost flights on DC-10-30 N12061 (June 1985, the sharpest dated photo, side-on) on shapes/DC10.json, with the 727-200 (N79750, N79743, 1984) and the DC-9-10 measured as types and the DC-9-30/-50, MD-80, 737-200 and A300 fitted. The scheme is Saul Bass's of 1968 and is the same on dated photos from 1968, 1980, 1982, 1984 and 1985; by late 1986 a variant appears (on the A300s) with the fin's meatball in red-orange and an italic title, and the 1991 globe scheme replaced it; the 'to' date is that change, approximate. In 1985 there are only two stripes, gold over red: no separate orange line was found on any photo (the 'red' reads orange-red on the 1984 slides and crimson on the 1985 DC-10's). Every stripe edge is a level line in meters from the nose to the tail, sampled at the body profile's own points so it draws straight: on the DC-10 the gold from 1.355 m to 0.88 m above the centerline and the red from there to -0.21 m, read off the photo against the crown at 31.9 px/m in two places along the cabin (within 0.05 m). The red runs on to the tail cone under the tailplane (and on the 727 behind the side engines, as its 1968 photo shows too). Aft, the gold's top edge leaves its line at 39.4 m and rises straight, 0.42 m per meter, to the crown, so the upper tail, the centre engine's nacelle and the fin are gold, with a white band 0.4 m wide along the fin's leading edge, carried down over the centre engine's intake. The fin's meatball is 3.3 m across (it reads 3.55 m wide by 3.07 m tall). The 727 isn't the drawnOn type because its meatball sits half over the S-duct's fairing, below the fin's root, which doesn't carry to fins without a tail engine; it's measured as types.B722. 'CONTINENTAL' is upright on the 1984-85 photos (the later variant's is italic), an extended sans close to Helvetica Bold Extended, its capitals 0.63 m on the DC-10 and 0.40 m on the 727; the small red meatball is ahead of it and the flag behind on both sides. The marks named (CO1934/meatball, CO1934/us-flag) are described, not included. Colours are readings off slides, not Continental's specification. The registration (red, under the windows aft) and the DC-10s' names under the cockpit aren't drawn. No 747 entry: Continental's 747s on dated photos (1987) wear another scheme, and no photo of a 747 in this one in the 1980s was found.

B722.note: 727-200 N79750 (June 1984), checked on N79743 (May 1984): the gold from 1.32 m to 0.80 m and the red to -0.21 m, read against the windows (0.39-0.73 m) at 19 px/m (within about 0.1 m). The red runs on to the tail cone behind the side engines. The gold's front edge rises from its top at 33.0 m parallel to the fin's leading edge (its first stretch), about 1.0 m behind it, over the S-duct's fairing and up the fin, so the white leading-edge band is wider than the DC-10's. The fin's meatball sits low, mostly over the S-duct's fairing, about 2.5 m across. White nacelles with bare metal lips. Title capitals 0.40 m, 4.9 m long.
